questions.question: Why does `useNotes` track a separate `loaded` boolean instead of just checking if `notes.length === 0`?
options: It doesn't matter, both are equivalent
Because AsyncStorage reads are asynchronous, so an empty array could mean 'genuinely no notes' or 'still loading' — loaded distinguishes the two
loaded is required syntax for AsyncStorage
It makes the component re-render faster
questions.explanation: Without a distinct loading flag, the UI would briefly show 'No notes yet' on every launch before the real data arrives from AsyncStorage, even for a user with existing notes.

questions.question: Why use `FlatList` instead of mapping over `notes` inside a `ScrollView`?
options: ScrollView cannot render lists at all
FlatList only renders items on or near screen, which keeps scrolling smooth as the list grows, unlike ScrollView which renders everything upfront
FlatList is required for AsyncStorage to work
questions.explanation: ScrollView renders all its children immediately regardless of what's visible; FlatList virtualizes rendering, which matters a lot once a list has more than a handful of items.

questions.question: Why does `keyExtractor` use `item.id` instead of the array index?
options: A stable, content-based key lets FlatList correctly recycle and track row components across re-renders and reordering, avoiding flicker
keyExtractor is purely cosmetic and has no effect on behavior
questions.explanation: This is the same stable-key principle from the React fundamentals course — an index-based key breaks identity tracking whenever items are deleted, inserted, or reordered.

questions.question: What does the project's hook design (notes/addNote/updateNote/deleteNote as the public API) make easy to swap out later?
options: Nothing — the storage mechanism is hard-coded throughout the app
The underlying storage (AsyncStorage) for something like SQLite, since screens only ever interact with the hook's public API, not AsyncStorage directly
questions.explanation: Because screens never call AsyncStorage directly, swapping the persistence layer only requires changing the inside of useNotes — callers are unaffected, which is the whole point of the abstraction.
